newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania upbeat about NATO membership prospects.
newsitem.headline: Romania upbeat about NATO membership prospects.

text.p: Romanian officials said on Wednesday their drive for early admission to NATO had been well received and pledged to press ahead with a high-profile campaign to win over Western countries.

But northern neighbour Ukraine said it expected the Balkan state to work at the same time towards completing a friendship pact between Bucharest and Kiev, bedevilled by long-standing disputes dating from World War Two.
Romania is one of several former Soviet satellites in east Europe trying to shake off the perception of being outsiders in the stakes for joining NATO's initial expansion.
NATO is likely to begin its admission process next year despite Russian opposition with favourites for early membership being Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Sorin Ducaru said trips last week to Brussels, London and Paris by Foreign Minister Teodor Melescanu and other envoys had produced positive results.
"France offered firm support for Romania's membership from the beginning of the expansion process," Ducaru told Reuters.
"For Britain, the keyword is 'opening' -- Britain's opening to Romania's move to be included in the first expansion. Britain said there were no pre-conceived ideas."
Defence Minister Gheorghe Tinca was due to resume the campaign this week by travelling to Germany, whose influence could be vital to any membership bid.

But Ukraine's ambassador to Romania said the former Soviet republic wanted to impress on Bucharest the importance of the bilateral treaty -- especially after Romania's signature of a similar treaty with Hungary despite protracted difficulties.

"Concluding such treaties is one of the criteria NATO uses for new membership. Ukraine considers a political treaty with Romania as one of the necessary conditions," Olexander Chaly said by telephone.
"We see no difference in a treaty between Romania and Hungary, which we understand to be an important element for this country, and one between Romania and Ukraine."
Talks on a treaty have stalled on Romania's insistence that Ukraine denounce the Nazi-Soviet pact which enabled the Soviet Union to seize large chunks of Romanian territory in 1940.
Romania says it has no claim on Northern Bukovina, Southern Bessarabia and Serpent Island -- a tiny outcropping of islands off the Black Sea Coast.
Fresh talks are scheduled later this month in Kiev and Chaly said he was confident a treaty could be ready by the new year -- after next month's Romanian general election.
Slovakia pursued its membership campaign, with a defence ministry official in Bratislava saying the government was undaunted by suggestions that it was not among the favourites.

Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas told NATO ambassadors in Brussels his Baltic state also deserved to be included. Ukraine, wary of its proximity to Russia, says it has no plans to join NATO but seeks a "special relationship".
